item.figure_description:
Six 2D polygon outlines arranged in two rows of three:
- Top row:
  - P: a scalene triangle with a horizontal base.
  - Q: a four-sided quadrilateral resembling a trapezoid, with horizontal top and bottom sides (top shorter than bottom) and slanted right side.
  - R: a diamond/rhombus shape (a square rotated 45 degrees).
- Bottom row:
  - S: a very wide, flat obtuse triangle with a horizontal top-like orientation and a vertex pointing down.
  - T: an isosceles trapezoid with parallel horizontal top and bottom edges (top shorter than bottom).
  - U: a wide obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge and a vertex pointing downwards.

- Interior: 2 dots are spaced along the middle horizontal level between the left indented vertex and the right boundary.

reference_items.figure_description: At the top of the item is a solid black equilateral triangle with a horizontal base and its apex pointing directly upward. Below the question is an outline of a concave seven-sided polygon (heptagon) composed of five contiguous equilateral triangles of the same size as the tile above. slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
